column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/release-pipeline.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. release-pipeline is the mega-pipeline: one caller-side
# file that fans a single trigger out to four reusable workflows. Its whole job
# is SELECTION — it contains no steps of its own, so every one of its defects is
# a selection defect, and selection is exactly what nothing was asserting when
# graphql-synthesizer bumped, tagged, pushed and published nothing on a green
# tick. Four jobs, and each is a different delivery path that has to fire on the
# right event and only on the right event:
#   pre-merge  -> pre-merge-gate.yml   (PR only)
#   security   -> security-gate.yml    (PR + schedule)
#   release    -> auto-release.yml     (push only)     <- the delivery path
#   container  -> container-stack.yml  (push + both container inputs)
# The three context paths every condition reads — github.event_name,
# inputs.build-container, inputs.image — are therefore declared in EVERY row,
# including rows where a value is irrelevant to the outcome. An undeclared path
# is an error by design: a row that omits one is an incomplete case wearing a
# confident verdict.
# github.event_name here is the CALLER's event, not this file's. This workflow
# has no `on:` of its own beyond `workflow_call`, so the caller's push /
# pull_request / schedule trigger is what every condition is really reading.
# THE PRIVACY POSTURE IS NOT ASSERTABLE HERE, and rows push-public-* /
# push-private-* exist to say so rather than to leave it silently unexamined.
# The `&& !github.event.repository.private` guard that made graphql-synthesizer
# silent lives one level down, inside auto-release.yml; this workflow's own
# conditions never read repository.private, so `release` selects identically on
# a public and a private repo and the no-publish decision happens after the
# selection this table can see. The two rows below declare that key purely to
# make the pair legible — the linter does not evaluate it, because nothing in
# this file references it. The real privacy assertion is
# `auto-release.cases.tsv`; do not read a green run here as evidence that a
# private repo was correctly withheld, or that a public one actually shipped.
# Reusable-workflow `with:`/`secrets:` propagation into a called workflow's own
# conditions is likewise not modelled, so a job selected here can still skip
# every job inside the workflow it calls.
# ── PR: the two gates run, nothing ships ───────────────────────────────────
pr-opened
# Same PR on a repo that DOES publish an image. Pins that the container inputs
# being set is not on its own enough to put a build on a pull request — the
# event check has to carry it, and `container` also inherits release's skip
# through needs-propagation.
pr-on-a-container-repo
# ── schedule: the weekly security sweep, and ONLY that ─────────────────────
# pre-merge must not fire (it is a PR gate with nothing to gate) and release
# must not fire (a cron tick is not a merge, and a scheduled release would tag
# and publish unattended).
scheduled-security-sweep
# THE ROW THAT MUST STAY GREEN. A merge on a fully-configured repo runs the
# release AND the container build. If either ever stops selecting, this repo
# stops shipping while every run still reports success — the exact shape of the
# defect this sweep exists to close.
push-public-releases-and-builds-image
# Same merge on a PRIVATE repo. Identical selection, deliberately: this file is
# visibility-blind and the privacy guard is inside auto-release.yml (see the
# header). Pinning the pair keeps a future reader from "fixing" the asymmetry
# they expect to find here, and keeps the absence documented instead of unseen.
push-private-selects-identically
# The default caller: `build-container` and `image` left at their workflow_call
# defaults. Release runs, no container is built, and that is correct — most
# consumers of this pipeline ship a crate, not an image.
push-default-caller-no-container
# Half-configured, both directions. Each of these is a plausible caller typo
# that produces a green run with no image, so each gets its own row: the toggle
# on with no image to build, and an image named with the toggle never flipped.
# Skipping is the intended behaviour of both — the point is that it is now
# WRITTEN DOWN, so a genuine regression in `container` cannot hide behind the
# same silence.
push-container-on-but-image-empty
push-image-set-but-container-off
